import pytest
from your_module import run_length_encode  # Replace with the actual module name


class TestRunLengthEncode:
    """Unit tests for run_length_encode function."""

    # ---------- Happy path and edge cases ----------
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "input_str, expected",
        [
            # Empty string
            ("", []),
            # Single character
            ("a", [("a", 1)]),
            # Two identical characters
            ("aa", [("a", 2)]),
            # Two different characters
            ("ab", [("a", 1), ("b", 1)]),
            # Multiple groups
            ("aaabbbcc", [("a", 3), ("b", 3), ("c", 2)]),
            # All distinct
            ("abc", [("a", 1), ("b", 1), ("c", 1)]),
            # Alternating pairs
            ("aabbcc", [("a", 2), ("b", 2), ("c", 2)]),
            # Digits
            ("111222333", [("1", 3), ("2", 3), ("3", 3)]),
            # Spaces
            ("   ", [(" ", 3)]),
            # Newline characters
            ("a\n\nb", [("a", 1), ("\n", 2), ("b", 1)]),
            # Mixed case (case-sensitive)
            ("aAaA", [("a", 1), ("A", 1), ("a", 1), ("A", 1)]),
            # Unicode characters
            ("ééé", [("é", 3)]),
            # Long run of identical characters
            ("a" * 1000, [("a", 1000)]),
        ],
    )
    def test_happy_path_and_edge_cases(self, input_str, expected):
        """Test typical inputs and edge cases."""
        assert run_length_encode(input_str) == expected

    # ---------- Error cases and special inputs ----------
    def test_none_input(self):
        """
        Test that None input returns an empty list.
        (The function treats None as falsy and returns []).
        """
        assert run_length_encode(None) == []

    def test_integer_input_raises_type_error(self):
        """Test that passing an integer raises a TypeError (no len())."""
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            run_length_encode(123)

    def test_list_input_by_duck_typing(self):
        """
        The function works on any sequence that supports indexing and
        comparison. This test verifies that behaviour for a list of integers.
        """
        assert run_length_encode([1, 1, 2, 3, 3]) == [(1, 2), (2, 1), (3, 2)]
